title: iOS, iPadOS, and tvOS: Screen and controls
lead: Use the running Apple app to choose a source, change playback settings, compare controls and inspect applied code. Follow operations with SDK state and events. iPhone/iPad and tvOS differences are explained beside the relevant steps.

items.label: Implementation guide: PlayerConfig, source configuration, UI changes and FAQ

blocks.text: Preparation and build
Build and launch Showcase-iOS or Showcase-tvOS using Local setup and licenses. This chapter starts with the running app; Swift integration and UI source changes are in the implementation guide.

blocks.title: Display language
blocks.text: The app follows the system or per-app language preference. This guide shows the English app. SDK identifiers, code and returned data retain their original spelling. Standard Player controls also depend on SDK and system language settings.

blocks.title: Appearance and guide images
blocks.text: The app follows the device’s Light or Dark appearance. This guide uses Light appearance for iPhone, iPad and Apple TV. On iOS/iPadOS choose Settings → Display & Brightness → Light; on tvOS choose Settings → General → Appearance → Light. The wide Apple TV images are tvOS screens, rather than an iPhone in landscape. Device appearance changes the app’s workspace; Theme changes the controls over the video.
Suggested screen workflow

Source is beside the playback preview; iOS and iPadOS also offer Theme. tvOS uses System UI with remote focus, Select and the system keyboard. The workspace tabs open configuration in Settings, Operations/State/Events/Host in APIs, applied settings in Code, and tracks/tools/diagnostics in More.

rows: Tap Settings, APIs, Code or More.
Focus a tab with the remote and open it with Select.
Choose Default, Sports, Live (DVR) or Cinema. Advanced settings also expose System/Subtitle.
Uses native System UI, with no Web UI theme selector.
Touch, menus and the software keyboard.
Directional input, Select and the system keyboard. Back/Menu within the editor returns to the current tab.

blocks.text: On iOS and iPadOS, the compact preview leaves room for editing. Use the adjacent Play/Pause button and Expand player or Collapse player. Expanding while typing closes the keyboard. The current source and playback position stay in place.

blocks.caption: Settings with Source and Title selected. Choose another field from the selector on the right. Reset to applied and Apply stay at the bottom. iPhone simulator.

items: Select VOD HLS under Source and press Play. On iOS/iPadOS, Expand player also reveals Position. Check that the picture and position advance.
In Settings → Start position, enter 5 seconds for Start offset and choose Start for Offset reference. Check Reload source, apply, and compare the starting position.
In Settings → Playback, enable Autoplay and keep Start muted on. Check Recreate player and reload source, apply, and confirm automatic muted playback.
On iOS/iPadOS, switch Theme to compare the controls. Each switch reloads the source. tvOS has no theme selector.
Use Settings → Tracks for initial tracks and Player UI for Video scaling. More → Tracks shows the current selections.
Inspect applied settings in Code. Use APIs → Operations, State and Events to compare a call with its result.
Play Live HLS and wait for a rewind window, then open More → Live controls. Use a negative offset to rewind and Live edge to return. The event log is in More → Diagnostics.

blocks.text: Changing Theme reloads the selected source. It does not retain the previous position or playing/paused state.

blocks.title: Do not add DASH to the Apple catalog
blocks.text: Apple playback accepts HLS and Progressive MP4; the catalog provides HLS. Use Web or Android for DASH comparisons. The implementation guide covers source-format constraints.

blocks.caption: The tvOS simulator during remote-control verification. Use Play/Pause on the remote and move focus to configuration.

blocks.text: Edit source and playback configuration

items: Choose Settings, Category and Setting. The draft summary, Reset to applied (Reset at enlarged text sizes) and Apply stay outside the editor. tvOS uses the remote and system keyboard.
In Source, enter an absolute HTTP(S) URL and choose HLS or Progressive MP4. Title and Poster URL are optional; clearing them removes those values.
In Start position, choose an offset in seconds and its reference. Clear Start offset to restore the SDK default.
Choose a field in Playback, Player UI or Quality and buffer. Read its units and accepted inputs.
Read the summary and pending action, then Apply. Invalid input disables Apply; Show field opens the affected input. The editor remains open after Apply and reports the changed settings.

blocks.text: Source changes reload playback; Player or view configuration changes recreate the player. Playback restarts at the configured offset according to Autoplay, without retaining the old position or playing state. The implementation guide explains settings and defaults.

blocks.title: Apply and reset
blocks.text: Apply is disabled when the draft matches the applied values. Reset to applied changes only the draft; it does not restore defaults or restart playback. Categories and tabs retain drafts. A source preset resets source fields and initial tracks while retaining Player settings. Applied settings last for the current app session.

items: After Apply, choose Code to inspect the active Player, Source and UI values. On iPhone and iPad, Wrap lines is on by default; turn it off when comparing original line lengths. tvOS always wraps code lines.
Edit a draft without applying and confirm that Code stays unchanged. iPhone/iPad supports Copy code and text selection; tvOS provides focusable wrapped code lines without clipboard integration.

On tvOS, press Back/Menu while reading code or using an editor to return focus to the current workspace tab. Use Left/Right and Select to switch tabs. Back/Menu on the tab bar retains its system behavior.

blocks.caption: Code shows the applied Swift configuration with Wrap lines enabled. Draft edits are excluded and the license is replaced with YOUR_PLAYER_KEY. The compact preview and its playback controls remain visible.
Applied Swift configuration on tvOS. Focusable wrapped lines support remote reading; this TV host has no clipboard integration.

blocks.text: Additional SDK settings

items: Choose Settings → Advanced SDK. Search by API name or choose an SDK group, then use Setting to open one property’s editor. The info button, SDK setting details, opens the property description, accepted values and units.

Turn on Override for that property. The value input is separate: depending on its type, it is a switch, enumeration, text field, structured JSON or callback body. Read accepted values and units. Disabling the override restores the basic form value or SDK default after Apply.

Read the pending action and Apply. Source settings reload the source; Player and view settings recreate the player. Invalid values leave active settings unchanged. Code displays the Swift configuration from the applied values.
In APIs → State, select Refresh to check the loaded source, tracks or player value. An option may affect playback only with matching content, a service or a supported device.

blocks.text: Edit the subtitle list in SourceConfig.tracks. Apply the illustrated example, then refresh Player.availableSubtitles in APIs → State. The implementation guide explains its input format and track constraints.

blocks.caption: SourceConfig.tracks in the iPhone editor. Each object describes a subtitle track, with accepted properties listed below the input.

blocks.text: This manual track has no subtitle file or cues. After Apply, use the cue APIs to add timing and content, then select the track. For a workflow shared by iOS and tvOS, use subtitles within HLS.

blocks.caption: Player.availableSubtitles after applying the subtitle list. The result contains the tracks and identifiers returned by the actual SDK.

blocks.text: Editable callbacks

items: Search for a callback such as LabelingConfig.audioLabel and enable its override. Read the description of input and the required return type.
Enter a function body, such as return 'GUI ' + input.label; for this label callback, then Apply. Editing the draft alone does not install or invoke it.
Use content that causes the SDK to call the function. In APIs → State, filter Callback and refresh. Calls and failures distinguish an installed function from one actually invoked by the SDK.
Inspect Code. To restore the SDK behavior, disable the override and Apply.

blocks.caption: The audio-label callback accepts a JavaScript body that returns a replacement for the label in input.
State after the SDK invoked the applied audio-label body. Counts are shown without callback payloads.

blocks.title: Execution and fallback
blocks.text: Syntax errors disable Apply. After applying, trigger the SDK callback and inspect calls and failures. Execution errors or invalid results use the fallback shown by the field. The implementation guide covers supported syntax and code reuse.
Initial tracks and video scaling

items: Select HLS with audio and subtitle tracks. In Settings → Tracks, enter an audio language such as de-AT and choose Automatic, Off or Preferred language for subtitles. Enter a subtitle language for Preferred language.
Apply and wait for loading and playback readiness. Inspect More → Tracks and the visible captions. A missing language keeps the default selection.
In Player UI, choose Fit, Fill (crop) or Stretch and apply. Different video/view aspect ratios make the effect easier to compare.

blocks.caption: The initial audio-language field on iPad. This is a source-local app preference applied during startup, rather than a PlayerConfig language property.
The video-scaling setting on iPad. The selected value is passed to SDK StyleConfig.scalingMode when the player is recreated.
The initial audio-language setting on tvOS. Select the field with the remote and enter a language code using the system keyboard.
Fit, Fill (crop) and Stretch are native focusable choices in the tvOS form.

blocks.text: Clear the audio language and choose Automatic subtitles, then Apply, or select a source preset to remove initial track preferences. Restore Fit and Apply if scaling has changed.
When something does not work

items: If playback fails, check the Player license, allowed bundle identifier, connectivity and reference source. See the integration FAQ for details.
If HLS rewind controls are disabled, start playback and wait for a rewind window.
A paused position that leaves the live retention window returns toward the live edge. Inspect state and events when checking behavior after the live stream ends.

items.label: Implementation FAQ: configuration and UI issues

blocks.text: Use the SDK default player controls
Default provides normal playback, timeline seeking and the source's track menus. Scroll inside the player menu to reach options below its viewport.

items: On iPhone/iPad select Default; tvOS uses native System UI. Load media with the audio/subtitle tracks you want to compare and start playback. On tvOS use the remote’s Play/Pause command.
Pause, resume and drag the timeline. In Settings, choose a speed preset or an available audio/subtitle track.
Use APIs → Operations for an arbitrary volume or speed value. Choose Native PlayerView to try fullscreen and view APIs.

blocks.text: The default menu offers speed presets. Its speaker button can toggle mute without providing a numeric volume slider. Use API operations to try other accepted values.

On iOS/iPadOS, Allow live rewind controls changes the embedded live seek bar and app quick actions immediately without reloading media. On-demand seeking remains available. tvOS uses native System UI; its public API cannot switch only live rewind controls at runtime, so this preference is disabled with a reason. Use Settings → Playback → Live time shift and Apply to change the SDK creation-time setting.
Run APIs and read their results

In APIs → Operations, choose the target and check its name beside Run API. Search only filters candidates; it does not change the target automatically. State reads current values, Events records notifications, and Host selects the player factory and video presentation. Operations requiring a source, active ad, current track or native view are disabled while prerequisites are missing, with a reason beside the selected operation. Run API checks again before dispatch. Source changes preserve the operation and argument draft.

blocks.title: Read snapshots and event history
blocks.text: Current SDK snapshot is a read taken with Refresh. Check the read time and Player/Source owner of related state after an operation. Events retains the latest 120 API names, owners and SDK timestamps. For asynchronous actions, correlate completion events with state.

blocks.title: Thumbnail rendering
blocks.text: renderThumbnail draws asynchronously into a UIView. After the call, inspect the rendered image as well as the returned metadata.

items: Open APIs → Operations, filter Player.volume and choose it. Enter a whole number such as 50 within 0–100 and Run API. Read argument errors. Code displays the Swift call for the current valid arguments; Arguments returns to the inputs.

blocks.caption: Operations with Volume selected. Run API stays below the editor, and Related SDK state shows the value read from the player after the call. iOS simulator.

items: Switch to State, filter Player.volume and choose Refresh. Compare the actual value with your command. Refresh after later operations as needed. When finished, use the same operation to restore the previous value.

blocks.caption: State filtered to Player.volume. Refresh reads the value from the current SDK player; it is separate from submitting an operation.

items: In Events, clear the old entries and enable recording before the next trial. Use Play/Pause or a supported seek, then inspect event name, owner and SDK timestamp. For asynchronous actions, also check the completion event and resulting position.

Filter by event or owner. Typed listeners and Combine publishers select the subscription method. Registration alone does not mean an event occurred; Player and Source listeners can report the same playback event.

blocks.caption: The tvOS API inspector uses the same Operations, State and Events workflow with remote focus and Select.

blocks.text: Choose the video presentation

Choose APIs → Host, then use Host setting to choose Presentation or Player factory. Presentation offers SDK SwiftUI, SDK SwiftUI with bindings, Native PlayerView, AVPlayerLayer and AVPlayerViewController. A change recreates the player and reloads the applied source; SDK SwiftUI is the default. Host settings are separate from the operation picker.

rows: Change Picture-in-Picture and scaling bindings; inspect availability.
Run fullscreen and Picture-in-Picture operations and inspect view events.
Compare a registered video layer with the separate app controls and scaling.
Compare AVKit controls and Show AVKit playback controls.

blocks.text: Check Picture-in-Picture and remote-playback availability on a supported OS/device. Choose Presentation code in Host setting to inspect the selected view, layer or controller integration.
Choose SDK SwiftUI to restore the default presentation. For PiP, check enabled, available and active state separately.
Playlist drafts
blocks.summary: Edit source drafts separately from the active SDK playlist.

blocks.text: Open More → Tools → Playlist, add a copy of the applied source, and edit each source’s URL, offsets, metadata, subtitles and DRM. Editing a draft does not change SDK playback. Use Load, Add or Insert in Operations, then inspect the SDK playlist in State and Code. Applying the main player configuration restores its normal single-source setup.

items.label: Initial track selection for preloaded sources

blocks.text: SharePlay sessions

items: Choose More → SharePlay, then Sessions in the SharePlay selector. Listen for sessions receives actual sessions created by the operating system; none is joined automatically.

Choose Activity. With a loaded source, Activate current source activity asks the OS to activate its SharePlay activity. It shares the source URL and title, so choose an appropriate source before activation.
Choose Coordinate and select an actual OS session, then use Coordinate current player or Coordinate and join. Participating players need matching SourceConfig.options.sharePlayIdentifier values.
Refresh group state reads session state and participant count. In Coordinate, Leave selected session requests this app’s departure; in Sessions, Stop listening only stops observation.

blocks.text: Joining requires an eligible OS session. Choose Code to inspect the public API call. The implementation guide covers OS eligibility and signing requirements.
Offline HLS on iOS and iPadOS
Verify downloads and cached playback on a physical iPhone or iPad. This panel is unavailable on tvOS. The implementation guide records the simulator validation scope.

items: Apply an on-demand HLS source and DRM settings, then open More → Tools → Offline HLS. Live HLS has no finite download.
In Section → Manager, set the Wi-Fi restriction and minimum free space. Save initialization options using SDK defaults or OfflineConfig.
After first setup or changing startup options, fully close and reopen the app. Apply HLS and DRM settings again, then reopen Offline HLS.

In Asset, set an identifier and Select applied HLS source as offline asset. Fetch available audio and subtitle tracks, then choose them in Download settings → Tracks. Reuse the identifier when addressing the same asset later.
In Operations, choose a download action and Run offline API. Inspect progress, offlineState and Events, then wait for completion.

In Cached playback, choose whether to restrict playback to cached media, then Create OfflineSourceConfig and Load cached source. Recreate OfflineSourceConfig before loading if you change that restriction.

blocks.caption: The offline inspector lists actual SDK audio/subtitle tracks and their download actions.

blocks.text: Suspend, resume, cancel and delete affect the selected asset. Selecting another asset leaves its download running; use suspend or cancel to stop it. Delete removes its cache. Applying settings or reloading the source returns cached playback to the remote source.

blocks.title: Offline operation details
blocks.text: Refresh offline state reads progress and offlineState. Events retains up to 80 names, selected-asset owners and SDK timestamps. Compare the submission result with the completed state.
Google Cast on iOS and iPadOS

items: Open More → Tools → Google Cast. In Section → Receiver settings, use Setting to enter the receiver application ID and optional urn:x-cast:… namespace, then choose background sessions, discovery and receiver-stop behavior.
In Section → Operations, choose initializeCasting(options:) and Run Cast API before enabling RemoteControlConfig.isCastEnabled in Settings → Advanced SDK. Empty receiver fields use SDK defaults.
Initialization is process-wide. Changing initialized options saves them for the next full app launch. Close and reopen the app; recreating a player alone does not replace Cast.

In Section → State, Refresh Cast state inspects initialization, availability and connection separately. Operations contains receiver playback, messaging and listener registration; Events shows received notifications.

blocks.caption: Receiver and discovery options in the Google Cast inspector. They configure the app process's startup.
The sender is initialized; receiver availability and connection are separate state values.

blocks.title: Receiver requirements
blocks.text: Receiver playback requires a compatible Cast device, local-network permission and suitable media. The tvOS app does not include Google Cast. See the implementation guide for custom-receiver registration.

Use remove(listener:) to stop recording notifications. Disable automatic initialization next launch does not uninitialize the current sender. End the receiver session explicitly when needed, checking Stop receiver when ending session.

blocks.title: Cast event history
blocks.text: add(listener:) starts recording the latest 80 event names. Device names and message payloads are omitted. Check discovery, connection and playback in State and on the receiver.
Applied configuration code
Choose Code to retain the settings already sent to the SDK. Compare it before and after Apply. Unapplied edits are excluded and license values are placeholders.

Initial track preferences appear as one-time selection logic. This output is a reference for integration, not a complete independent app. Follow the implementation guide for configuration types, UI changes, callback resources, useful features and Analytics/Observability.
Analytics and Observability
blocks.summary: Connect collector configuration with session inspection in Dashboard.

blocks.text: For configured Analytics, choose PlayerFactory (with configured Analytics) under APIs → Host. Play a known source, then find its session in Bitmovin Dashboard Observability. The implementation guide covers licensing and investigation steps.
